title: Settings
subtitle: Sign-in, storage, logging, caching, and the model catalog. Infrastructure secrets stay in the environment.

access.title: Self-registration
access.subtitle: People can create their own console account from the sign-in page.
access.registrationHint: Off by default. New accounts get the Viewer role and must set up two-factor authentication. It is ignored while sign-in is limited to SSO.

updates.title: Updates
updates.subtitle: Compares this build with the releases published on GitHub for the same channel.
updates.hint: Asks the GitHub releases API at most every six hours and shows Update available in the top bar. Turn it off in networks without internet access.
updates.state: {state, select, available {Running {current}. {latest} is available.} current {Running {current}, the newest release.} other {Running {current}.}}

automatic.title: Automatic updates
automatic.subtitle: An updater container next to the app checks the image registry and restarts LLM Hub with new images.

env.title: Environment
env.subtitle: These values come from process env. They are not edited in the console.
env.item: {item, select, s3 {Object storage keys} oidc {OIDC client secret} smtp {Mail (SMTP_URL)} redis {Redis (REDIS_URL)} other {Setting}}
env.hint: Secrets come from the environment: S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID, S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET, SMTP_URL, and REDIS_URL.

general.description: Self-registration, update checks, and the server environment.

scim.title: SCIM provisioning
scim.subtitle: Your identity provider creates, updates, and blocks console users and groups through SCIM 2.0. Creating the token needs every permission because group rules can assign any role.
scim.issueDescription: {set, select, true {Confirm with your authenticator. The current token stops working immediately.} other {Confirm with your authenticator. The token is shown only once.}}
scim.revokeDescription: Confirm with your authenticator. SCIM requests fail until you create a new token.
scim.tokenHint: It is shown only once. Paste it into your identity provider as the bearer token.
scim.manageHint: Only users who hold every permission can create or revoke the SCIM token.
scim.mappingHint: Point your provider at /Users and /Groups below this URL. Groups use the same rules as single sign-on, and provisioned users land on the same account when they sign in.

signIn.description: Single sign-on with OpenID Connect, group to role rules, and SCIM provisioning. The owner always keeps password sign-in with two-factor authentication.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.subtitle: Connect an OpenID Connect identity provider. The client secret stays in the environment as OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET.
sso.enabledHint: {ready, select, true {OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET is set.} other {Set OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET in the environment first.}}
sso.issuerHint: The provider publishes /.well-known/openid-configuration below this URL.
sso.scopesHint: openid is always requested. Add groups when your provider needs a scope for the groups claim.

check.title: {state, select, ok {Issuer found} unsupported {Issuer found, but its signing algorithms are not supported} unreachable {Issuer not reachable} http {Discovery request failed} not_json {No discovery document} issuer_mismatch {Issuer does not match} entra_v1 {Microsoft Entra v1 endpoint} multi_tenant {Multi-tenant issuer} incomplete {Discovery document incomplete} other {Issuer check failed}}
check.found: {issuer} answers. The client authenticates with {method}. ID tokens are signed with {algorithms}.
check.tenantId: You entered a tenant domain. Sign-in verifies tokens against the tenant ID issuer {issuer}.
check.failed: {reason, select, http {The provider answered HTTP {status} for /.well-known/openid-configuration below this URL. Check the issuer path, such as the realm, tenant, or application.} not_json {The URL answers, but not with an OpenID Connect discovery document. Check that it points at the identity provider and not at a login page or a proxy.} issuer_mismatch {The discovery document names the issuer {issuer}. The issuer URL must match it exactly.} entra_v1 {{issuer} is the Microsoft Entra v1 endpoint. Append /v2.0 to the issuer URL: {suggestion}} multi_tenant {Microsoft Entra answers with a multi-tenant issuer for common and organizations. Use your Directory (tenant) ID: https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/v2.0.} incomplete {The discovery document lacks the authorization, token, or JWKS endpoint. LLM Hub needs all three.} other {This server could not connect to the provider. The check runs on the LLM Hub server, not in your browser: check the URL, DNS, firewalls, and outbound HTTPS from the server.}}

presets.name: {id, select, entra {Microsoft Entra ID} google {Google Workspace} okta {Okta} keycloak {Keycloak} authentik {authentik} auth0 {Auth0} other {Other OpenID Connect provider}}
presets.note: {id, select, entra {Use the Directory (tenant) ID, not the domain, common, or organizations: https://login.microsoftonline.com/TENANT_ID/v2.0. The issuer ends with /v2.0. Add the optional claims email and xms_edov, and a groups claim (group object IDs) or app roles (claim roles).} google {Google sends no groups. Everyone gets the default role; limit sign-in with allowed email domains.} okta {Use your Okta domain as issuer and add a groups claim filter to the ID token of the app.} keycloak {Issuer https://HOST/realms/REALM. Add a Group Membership mapper (claim groups, full group path off) to the client.} authentik {Use the OpenID configuration issuer of the application. The profile scope carries the groups claim.} auth0 {Issuer https://TENANT.auth0.com/. Groups or roles need an Action that adds a namespaced claim such as https://llmhub/roles.} other {Any provider with discovery, the authorization code flow, and PKCE.}}

checklist.title: Setup checklist
checklist.subtitle: Register LLM Hub at your provider as a confidential web application with the authorization code flow.
checklist.step: {step, select, callback {{position}. Register this redirect URI at the provider} secret {{position}. Put the client secret into OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET} client {{position}. checklist.secretHint: Restart LLM Hub after changing the environment. The secret is never stored in the database or shown here.

accounts.title: Accounts and roles
accounts.subtitle: Applies to console users who sign in with SSO or are provisioned through SCIM.
accounts.defaultRoleHint: New accounts get this role when no group rule matches.
accounts.defaultCompanyHint: New accounts are limited to this company. Existing accounts keep theirs.
accounts.domainsHint: Separate with commas. Leave empty to allow every account your provider signs in.

mapping.title: Group to role rules
mapping.subtitle: The first rule whose group matches decides the role. While rules exist, roles follow the identity provider at every sign-in and SCIM change. The owner is never changed.
mapping.claimHint: ID token claim that lists groups or roles, for example groups, roles, or realm_access.roles. SCIM groups match by display name or external ID.
mapping.empty: No rules yet. Everyone gets the default role.

ssoOnly.title: SSO only
ssoOnly.subtitle: Hide password sign-in for everyone except the owner.
ssoOnly.hint: {ready, select, true {Password sign-in, passkey sign-in, and self-registration stop for everyone except the owner, who keeps password and two-factor authentication as a fallback.} other {Finish the single sign-on setup first so nobody gets locked out.}}

matching.title: How accounts are matched
matching.body: Sign-in first looks for an account already linked to the subject at this issuer, then for an account whose SCIM external ID equals the subject or the Entra object ID, then for the verified email address. The first match is linked permanently. An account already linked to another subject of the same issuer is refused.

storage.description: Files, batch outputs, videos, and log archives go to S3-compatible storage when a bucket and keys are set. Otherwise they stay in Postgres.

Check the URL, port, and network.} AUTH {The access key was rejected.} SIGNATURE {The secret key or the region does not match.} DENIED {These keys may not write, read, or delete objects in this bucket.} NO_BUCKET {The bucket does not exist at this endpoint.} REGION {The bucket lives in another region or needs another endpoint.} MISMATCH {The object read back differs from the one written.} other {The storage answered with an error.}} {step, select, put {It failed while writing.} get {It failed while reading.} delete {It failed while deleting.} other {}} {status, select, none {} other {HTTP {status}.}}

keys.title: Access keys
keys.subtitle: Keys stay in the environment and are never shown or stored in the database.
keys.hint: Restart LLM Hub after changing S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID or S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.

budgetAlerts.title: Budget alerts
budgetAlerts.hint: Webhooks that subscribe to budget thresholds fire once per threshold when spend crosses it. Changes apply right away.
budgetAlerts.addHint: Between 1 and 100 percent of a budget.

logging.retentionHint: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} by default. 0 keeps request logs indefinitely. Spend, usage, audit, and security activity use their own retention.
logging.spendRetentionHint: 0 keeps finance spend events indefinitely, even if request logs expire.
logging.usageRetentionHint: Daily usage totals behind usage charts, chargeback, and reports. 0 keeps them indefinitely, even if spend events expire.
logging.auditRetentionHint: 0 keeps the console audit trail and rejected integration approvals indefinitely.
logging.securityRetentionHint: Account security changes of console users, such as sign-in methods, roles, blocks, and management keys, with IP addresses. {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} by default, 0 keeps them indefinitely.
logging.objectRetentionHint: Stored responses, batches, batch results, and videos. {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} by default, 0 keeps them indefinitely. Running batches are never deleted.
logging.fileRetentionHint: Files uploaded through /api/v1/files. 0 keeps them indefinitely.
logging.webhookSecretState: {set, select, true {A secret is stored. Enter a new one to replace it.} other {No secret stored}}
logging.archive: Archive request logs to object storage
logging.archiveHint: {ready, select, true {Each request log is also written as JSON under logs/requests/ in the configured bucket.} other {Set up object storage in the Storage tab first.}}
logging.alertsHint: Each webhook receives only the events selected for it. With a signing secret, requests carry X-LLMHub-Timestamp and X-LLMHub-Signature: sha256=HMAC(secret, timestamp.body).
logging.noWebhooks: No webhooks yet. Alerts are not delivered.
logging.eventLabel: {event, select, upstream_exhaustion {Upstream exhaustion} budget_threshold {Budget threshold} provider_models_changed {Provider models changed} spend_anomaly {Spend anomaly} key_expiring {Key expiring} key_blocked {Key blocked} pii_blocked {PII blocked} other {Event}}
logging.eventHint: {event, select, upstream_exhaustion {No healthy deployment answered, or the upstream returned 5xx or 429.} budget_threshold {A key, person, project, department, or company crossed a budget alert threshold.} provider_models_changed {The hourly sync found added or removed provider models.} spend_anomaly {A key or project spent far more in the last hour than it usually does at that hour.} key_expiring {A key expires within the warning window set under Alert rules.} key_blocked {Someone blocked a key in the console, the management API, or the assistant.} pii_blocked {The PII policy blocked a request. At most one alert per key every 15 minutes, without the request content.} other {}}
logging.formatLabel: {format, select, json {JSON} slack {Slack} teams {Microsoft Teams} other {Format}}
logging.formatHint: {format, select, json {JSON with id, event, message, source, and ts.} slack {Message for a Slack incoming webhook.} teams {Adaptive Card for a Teams workflow webhook.} other {}}
logging.rulesHint: When spend anomaly and key expiry alerts fire. Budget thresholds have their own section below.
logging.anomalyFactorHint: Alert when a key or project spends at least this many times its average for the same hour over the previous 7 days. 0 turns it off.
logging.anomalyMinCostHint: Smaller amounts never count as an anomaly.
logging.expiryDaysHint: Warn this many days before a key expires. 0 turns it off.
logging.contentSubtitle: Prompts and responses stored with each request log.
logging.contentHint: Turn it off for a single person in Users or for a single key in its key settings. While PII redaction is active, stored content is masked and every log shows the entities it found.
logging.contentRetentionHint: {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} by default. 0 keeps content as long as the request log. A lower value removes prompts and responses earlier and keeps the metadata. Integration tool executions store tool output and follow the shorter of both values.
logging.description: Alert webhooks and rules, request content, retention, and log archiving.

cache.ttlHint: 0 turns the cache off. Clients skip the cache with the x-hub-bypass-cache header or "cache": false.

store.title: Storage and lifetime
store.description: Responses are stored per key, model, and request body. Hits are free for the key and logged as response cache hits.
store.backend: {backend, select, redis {Redis, shared} memory {In memory} other {Redis unreachable}}
store.backendHint: {backend, select, redis {All app instances share the response cache, and it survives restarts. Responses stay in Redis until they expire.} memory {Each app process keeps its own response cache, which is emptied on restart. Set REDIS_URL to share it.} other {REDIS_URL is set, but Redis does not answer. Each app process uses its own memory cache until Redis is back.}}

semantic.title: Semantic matching
semantic.description: Answers a request from the response cache when only the last user message differs and means nearly the same. System prompt, earlier messages, model, and parameters must still match exactly.
semantic.enabledHint: {ready, select, true {Every cache miss first embeds the last user message. That adds latency and embedding cost.} other {Choose an embedding model first.}}
semantic.modelHint: Embeddings run on this alias with the calling key's routing rules and are billed to that key. Keys that may not use this model only get exact matches.
semantic.thresholdHint: Minimum cosine similarity. Lower values answer more requests but can return an answer to a different question.

stats.title: Response cache statistics
stats.hint: Counts requests that were eligible for the response cache, across all keys. Net savings are the cost of the original responses served again from the response cache, minus the embedding cost of semantic lookups. Provider prompt caching is not included.

cache.description: The gateway answers identical non-streaming chat requests from the same key with a stored response for the configured time. Provider prompt caching is separate.

jev.title: Model catalog
jev.subtitle: How the catalog groups provider models and when it routes new providers on its own.
jev.enabledHint: {ready, select, true {Runs during each catalog refresh and only checks models that are new or could not be grouped by name.} other {Enter an OpenRouter API key first.}}
jev.apiKeyState: {set, select, true {Stored. Leave empty to keep it.} other {sk-or-…}}
jev.apiKeyHint: Use a separate OpenRouter key so Jev costs stay apart from your provider connections. The key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
jev.modelHint: OpenRouter System One model id. jev-latest follows the newest release.
jev.clearKey: Remove the stored key and turn Jev off
jev.catalogHint: Results and refresh status are on the <link>Model catalog</link> page.
jev.autoRoutesHint: Default for every alias that does not set its own value. Only trusted providers that start offering a model are routed; own OpenAI-compatible servers are always turned on by hand.
jev.minConfidenceHint: Jev matches below this value are shown in the catalog but never routed on their own. Matches by name always count as certain.

knowledge.title: Knowledge bases
knowledge.subtitle: Defaults for vector stores created in the console or through /api/v1/vector_stores without their own models.
knowledge.embeddingHint: Used when a new knowledge base does not name an embedding model. Existing knowledge bases keep their model.
knowledge.dimensionsHint: 0 uses the model's native size. Applies only together with the default embedding model.
knowledge.ocrHint: Reads text from PDFs and images for knowledge bases without their own OCR model.
knowledge.rerankHint: Reorders search results for knowledge bases without their own rerank model.
knowledge.manageHint: Create knowledge bases and upload files under <link>Knowledge bases</link>.

catalog.description: How the catalog groups provider models, and the default models for knowledge bases.
